result.summary: Do not ship: rendering all notification text as HTML enables remote error messages to inject deceptive links.

findings.title: Remote error output can inject phishing links into notifications
findings.body: After a successful scan, a remote command can fail with output `Reconnect your account`. sshcp.py:155 carries command output into SshcpError; remote_scanner.py:85-87 wraps it as a recoverable ScannerError; scanner_process.py:90-94 and controller.py:633 propagate it into status. HeaderComponent at header.component.ts:96-108 then publishes it as notification text without escaping. This changed binding turns that previously literal text into a clickable attacker-controlled link. Angular's HTML sanitizer permits anchors and HTTPS hrefs, so script sanitization does not prevent this UI injection.
findings.recommendation: Keep notification text interpolated. If links are needed, represent them as separate validated fields and render explicit anchors. Add a regression test using the real template; the existing bell tests override it with the old interpolation.

next_steps: Restore text rendering and verify remote error markup remains literal.
